title: Persist the stranded implementation lane's merged state so its stale scope lock is released, without claiming Done

sha_binding.verified_source_note: The last non-proof commit on this branch after the sanctioned rebase onto current main. It carries the single canonical record-merge write this bundle describes. It is the anchor only because a file cannot contain its own SHA; post-merge rebinding sets merge_sha. merge_sha is explicitly null pre-merge rather than a branch SHA or a stand-in token.

premise_check.claim: The predecessor lane's file_scope_lock is held solely because its manifest status is a member of ACTIVE_LOCK_STATUSES. Recording the merge that actually happened moves it to merged, which is not a member, and that alone releases the lock.
premise_check.method: Read ACTIVE_LOCK_STATUSES, TRANSITIONS and assertManifestWriteIsSafe in scripts/ops/shared.ts. Reproduced the successor lane's admission refusal by executing ops:lane-start. Read the post-merge refusal in scripts/ops/scope-release.ts. Read the merge facts from the GitHub API. Reproduced the reconciler's misclassification by executing resolveMergedPrForLane with and without GitHub CLI authentication.
premise_check.result: Confirmed. ACTIVE_LOCK_STATUSES = {started, in_progress, in_review, blocked, parked, reopened}; merged is absent. The admission refusal reproduced with code file_scope_conflict on exactly scripts/ops/proof-schema.ts and scripts/ops/proof-schema.test.ts.

blocked — written to main by the scheduled reconciler at 2026-08-29T20:03:21Z in commit af2fa19e, after this branch was created

reconciler_misclassification.expected_rule: ghost_merged is checked first and blocked is ghost-eligible; it would have written status merged, bound commit_sha, and released locks with an honest 'NOT closed' receipt
reconciler_misclassification.why_it_did_not_fire: resolveMergedPrForLane shells out to gh, and the 'Reconcile stale lane manifests' step in .github/workflows/reconcile-stale-lanes.yml supplies no GH_TOKEN. Every failure mode returns null by design, so the ghost rule is silently inert and the lane fell through to the heartbeat rule.
reconciler_misclassification.run_log: [STRANDED] UTV2-1729: heartbeat_at 186.8h old (threshold: 24h) -> status -> blocked, truth_check_history appended (run 33272452230)
reconciler_misclassification.does_not_converge: the heartbeat rule preserves heartbeat_at, so it re-fires every 6h and appends another identical receipt; docs/06_status/lanes/UTV2-1512.json already carries 11, three from today
reconciler_misclassification.disposition: tracked separately and deliberately not fixed here; once this record lands the predecessor leaves ACTIVE_LOCK_STATUSES and therefore leaves the reconciler's candidate population

alternatives_rejected.blocked_or_parked: Both are members of ACTIVE_LOCK_STATUSES, so neither releases the lock. main demonstrated this directly: the reconciler wrote blocked and the successor lane's admission conflict was unchanged.
alternatives_rejected.widen_scope_release: scope-release refuses on a non-OPEN PR by design (scripts/ops/scope-release.ts:222-224). Those paths were genuinely modified by the merged PR, so releasing them post-merge would change what the safety mechanism means. Not authorized and not attempted.
alternatives_rejected.reopen_as_multi_pr_lane: Rejected: the predecessor's implementation is merged; reopening would misrepresent it as in flight.
alternatives_rejected.edit_TRANSITIONS: Rejected. Changing the lifecycle table to make this narrative true would be the wrong direction of fix. TRANSITIONS is unchanged and no production source was modified by this lane.

mutation_testing.reason: This lane adds no control and changes no code. Its entire functional content is one canonical-command-produced state record. There is no guard here whose failure condition could be inverted. The controls this record relies on — ACTIVE_LOCK_STATUSES membership, the TRANSITIONS table, and record-merge's refusal to fabricate a truth-check receipt — are pre-existing and owned by other lanes; each was verified by reading source and by observing the command's actual output rather than by asserting it.
mutation_testing.negative_observation_recorded: The admission conflict was reproduced by execution before this lane existed (code file_scope_conflict, overlapping_files exactly the two proof-schema paths). That is the failing condition this record is meant to clear, and it must be observed to clear after merge; if it does not, this lane's premise is wrong and that must be reported rather than overridden.

safety_posture.note: This lane records a merge that already happened. It does not close a lane, does not certify a lane Done, and does not repair the defect that stranded it.

known_gaps: No Codex invocation occurred. The lane is registered executor codex-cli, but the entire authorized implementation is one canonical command with no authored code, so it was run directly. The model-routing sidecar declares the lane's registered routing and deliberately omits codex_exit_code and codex_cli_version, which would assert a run that did not happen. Disclosed rather than papered over; re-registering the lane as Claude-executed is a PM call.

The two sanctioned writers disagree on blocked -> merged. assertStatusTransition refuses it; record-merge performs it, because the write guard abstains on non-settled on-disk statuses. Recorded, not resolved. Any future caller reasoning about lifecycle legality from TRANSITIONS alone will get a different answer than the one the tooling actually enforces.

The reconciler's read-auth defect is unfixed and systemic. It affects every merged-but-unclosed lane: the ghost rule is inert, so each is filed as stranded and driven to blocked. It also does not converge — the rule preserves heartbeat_at, so it re-fires every six hours and appends another identical receipt. docs/06_status/lanes/UTV2-1512.json already carries eleven, three from today. Tracked separately and deliberately not staffed here.

This unblocks admission; it does not prove the successor repair correct. After merge, the successor lane's ops:lane-start must be re-attempted and observed to succeed. If the predecessor still appears as a file_scope_conflict, this lane's premise is wrong and that must be reported, not overridden.

The predecessor is left in a state no automation will advance on its own. merged releases the lock but its closeout still fails on P10/R3, so it is reachable only by an explicit sanctioned closeout replay after the successor lands. Intended, but the record sits visibly incomplete in the interim and nothing will nag about it.
scope-release remains unusable post-merge. This lane routes around that rather than fixing it, so any future lane whose closeout fails after merge hits the same cycle and needs the same bridge.

The root control checkout carries untracked shadow copies of the predecessor's manifest and sync file that disagree with main. They are not repository truth, they blocked git pull --ff-only, and one early read in this session came from the shadow before the discrepancy was caught. They are preserved unmodified outside the repository pending separate classification; this lane neither restores nor deletes them.

sign_off.note: This bundle is evidence, not certification. The done-gate is ops:truth-check, and T1 authority is PM's.

transition_semantics.assert_status_transition_result: REFUSED — Illegal manifest status transition: blocked -> merged
transition_semantics.why: record-merge is a separate authoritative reconciliation operation, not an ordinary lifecycle step: it queries the real PR, requires it to be merged, reads GitHub's authoritative merge SHA, refuses a conflicting existing commit_sha, records merged, and stops there — no done, no passing receipt. Mechanically it writes through writeManifestAtPath, whose guard votes on transitions only when the on-disk status is settled (scripts/ops/shared.ts:1982); blocked is not settled, so the guard abstains rather than being overridden.
transition_semantics.claim_made_by_this_bundle: record-merge recovery semantics. This bundle does NOT claim blocked -> merged is an ordinary TRANSITIONS transition.
